---
applyTo: "**/database/**,**/db/migrations/**"
---

# Database Instructions

## Entity Conventions

### Base Classes
- `AuditableEntity`: Adds `createdAt`, `createdBy` (immutable)
- `ModifiableAuditableEntity`: Adds `modifiedAt`, `modifiedBy` (mutable)

### Entity Structure
```kotlin
@Entity
@Table(name = "example_table")
class ExampleEntity : ModifiableAuditableEntity() {
    
    @Id
    @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY)
    val id: Long = 0
    
    lateinit var name: String
    
    @ManyToOne
    @JoinColumn(name = "parent_id")
    lateinit var parent: ParentEntity
    
    @OneToMany(mappedBy = "example", cascade = [CascadeType.ALL])
    val children: MutableList<ChildEntity> = mutableListOf()
}
```

## Repository Patterns
```kotlin
@Repository
interface ExampleRepository : JpaRepository<ExampleEntity, Long> {
    
    fun findByName(name: String): ExampleEntity?
    
    @Query("SELECT e FROM ExampleEntity e WHERE e.parent.id = :parentId")
    fun findByParentId(parentId: Long): List<ExampleEntity>
}
```

### Underscore Navigation
Use underscores to traverse relationships in derived query method names:
```kotlin
fun findByPrimaryLandlord_BaseUser_Id(userId: String): List<PropertyOwnership>
fun existsByIsActiveTrueAndAddress_Uprn(uprn: Long): Boolean
```

### Custom Search Repositories
For text search, use the interface + implementation pattern:
```kotlin
interface PropertyOwnershipSearchRepository {
    fun searchMatching(searchTerm: String, localCouncilId: Int): Page<PropertyOwnership>
}

class PropertyOwnershipSearchRepositoryImpl(
    private val entityManager: EntityManager,
) : PropertyOwnershipSearchRepository {
    // Uses native SQL with pg_trgm for text search
    // Dual index strategy (GIN for small results, GIST for large)
}
```

The main repository extends both `JpaRepository` and the custom search interface:
```kotlin
@Repository
interface PropertyOwnershipRepository :
    JpaRepository<PropertyOwnership, Long>,
    PropertyOwnershipSearchRepository { }
```

## Flyway Migrations

### Naming Convention
`V<major>_<minor>_<fix>__<descriptive_name>.sql`

Examples:
- `V1_0_0__create_landlord_table.sql`
- `V1_1_0__add_property_compliance.sql`
- `V1_1_1__fix_column_type.sql`

### Migration Location
`src/main/resources/db/migrations/`

### Migration Content
```sql
-- V1_2_0__add_example_table.sql
CREATE TABLE example_table (
    id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    created_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    created_by VARCHAR(255),
    modified_at TIMESTAMP,
    modified_by VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE INDEX idx_example_name ON example_table(name);
```

### Reference Data in Migrations

Integration tests reset the database by truncating every table except `flyway_schema_history` and `local_council`.
If a migration inserts reference data that tests rely on, add that table to `PRESERVED_TABLES` in
`src/test/kotlin/uk/gov/communities/prsdb/webapp/testHelpers/IntegrationTestHelper.kt`, and update the list in
`docs/IntegrationTestReadMe.md`. Otherwise the data will be deleted before every test that resets the database.

A migration that renames a preserved table must update `PRESERVED_TABLES` too, or the renamed table will be
truncated. `IntegrationTestHelperTests` covers this.

### Audited Entities (Envers)

Landlord and property record entities are annotated `@Audited` (Hibernate Envers). Each has a `<table>_aud` table
holding one row per revision, linked to `audit_revision` (time, One Login subject identifier, letting agent access id,
scheduled task name). The audit log tracks changes to landlord and property data that we may show to system operators
and local council users.

Entities opt in to auditing, but every property of an audited entity is audited unless it is marked `@NotAudited`:

- Audit a new entity (`@Audited` plus a `<table>_aud` table) if it holds landlord or property data that users can
  change.
- When adding, renaming or retyping a column on an audited entity, either make the same change to its `_aud` table in
  the same migration or mark the property `@NotAudited`. Schema validation (`ddl-auto: validate`) fails at startup if
  they diverge.
- Mark a property `@NotAudited` when:
  - there is no reason to show its history, e.g. tokens and password hashes. If the change itself matters, record it in
    an audited column instead, like `LettingAgentAccess.passwordSetDate`
  - Hibernate never inserts it, e.g. columns set by triggers or generated by the database (`insertable = false,
    updatable = false`, like `PropertyOwnership.singleLineAddress`) or other `insertable = false` columns (like
    `ModifiableAuditableEntity.lastModifiedDate`). Envers writes each audit row as an insert, so would only store null
  - it is a collection of a non-audited entity, e.g. `PropertyOwnership.payments`
- Relations from an audited entity to a non-audited entity need
  `@Audited(targetAuditMode = RelationTargetAuditMode.NOT_AUDITED)`, which stores just the id.
- Envers only sees changes made through Hibernate. Bulk JPQL updates, native SQL and DB `ON DELETE CASCADE` are not
  audited, so delete audited child rows through JPA (e.g. `orphanRemoval`).

## Search with Trigrams
- Use `pg_trgm` extension for fuzzy text search
- See existing search implementations for patterns
